name: oc-time-report
description: Estimation-vs-logged-hours report over a period (independent of the AI-usage JSON). Tempo-worklog driven and TICKET-based with PER-AREA columns. Tickets are selected by their DATE (resolutiondate, else updated) in the window, and every worklog on a selected ticket counts (all-time, so per-ticket totals match Jira's aggregatetimespent). One row per ticket with a column group for each area (Backend/Frontend/QA) giving that area's main developer, Architect & Dev-lead estimates, total dev / logged / sub-bug hours, an AI flag, two time gains (Architect and Dev-lead, each with/without sub-bugs; every aggregate gain — Totals-by-area, per month, and the Arch-gain-by-month table — is computed over only the tickets carrying that estimate, so an unestimated ticket's logged hours never inflate it, while the Est/Logged columns still show full sums) and a sub-bug count; a single Arch-gain B/F/Q column (considering bugs) and a Logged+bug B/F/Q/OH column right after the Final flag; and closing Overhead d / Overhead % / Overhead people / Total log d columns. Overhead people (Architect/PO/DevOps/Consultant/management, roster area 'overhead') never count as an area developer — their hours go to the Overhead bucket, itemised per person with hours. Each area's main developer is its top contributor by dev-logged + own sub-bug-fixing hours (a token reviewer never wins). Every ticket carries a Date (resolutiondate, else updated) and is grouped by month; the HTML splits into five tabs (All, User Stories All, User Stories Final, Bugs Final, Bugs and Others), each with Totals-by-area overall + per month and the per-ticket matrix grouped by month. Per-ticket rows also carry a Fix ver column (the Jira Fix Version/s, all shown) right after Type. Totals-by-area (shown in days, 1 d = 8 h) is one row per area with a Project column, % (right after Total dev d; share of total logged) and % Sub-bug (sub-bug share of the area) columns, an Arch gain cell showing three with-bug gains (all / no-AI / AI, each with ticket count) and a single with-bug DL gain. The HTML has two live picklists — Project and Fix version (a Bug with several fix versions matches each) — that recompute the Totals and filter the per-ticket rows. Right after the Totals-by-area table the HTML shows an Arch-gain-by-month summary (rows = months; columns Backend/Backend AI/Frontend/Frontend AI/QA/QA AI/Overhead; each cell = Architect gain with sub-bugs + ticket count in parentheses; the Overhead column instead shows overhead's share of that month's total logged hours). Tempo is fetched with a persistent month-bucketed cache (only the recent ~45 days re-fetched each run). Also writes a second finished-User-Story per-developer summary (per area main dev, split by AI true/false, grouped by month). The roster is embedded (accountId -> name/area/role/active). HTML + CSV to ./docs/, named with the run date and the window start and end (time-report-<date>-<start>-<end>.{html,csv}). Jira via direct REST and Tempo per-user, both mandatory tokens; no Atlassian MCP.
